key_insight: OS-Helix trains a single computer-using agent to choose between GUI actions and code execution in one learned action space, instead of relying on prompt-level tool routing.
engineering_relevance: This makes desktop automation more robust for real-world workflows that mix visual interaction, files, scripts, and system state changes.
method: Built hybrid supervision by pairing desktop apps with authentic file artifacts to create executable Ubuntu states.
Used a decoupled instruction/evaluator pipeline so tasks can be verified by final state, regardless of whether the solution uses GUI or code.
Cold-started with SFT on filtered hybrid data, then improved with online RL using Step-balanced GSPO to avoid long code traces dominating optimization.
evidence_signal: On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieved relative gains of 35.0% and 33.7% over matched baselines, and OS-Helix-27B-RL reached 66.44% success after a 42.9% improvement.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality executable desktop states and careful action-step balancing, so data construction and training stability may be challenging to reproduce at scale.
paper_title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
